title: Five shifts to rethink urban heat assessment and action
summary:
npj Urban Sustainability, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s42949-026-00451-9

Urban heat risk is intensifying, yet many cities continue to rely on static assessment approaches that inadequately capture how risk evolves spatiotemporally. We argue for a more dynamic and context-sensitive approach to urban heat assessment and action. We outline five shifts that recognize the interacting roles of hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and adaptive responses, and propose a decision-support framework to support more targeted, equitable, and actionable urban heat preparedness and adaptation.

title: Drought amplifies the psychological burden of war
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01882-z

Integrating georeferenced drought data from respondents’ pre-displacement regions with survey data from Syrian and Iraqi refugees, this study finds a stronger association between war exposure and post-traumatic stress among individuals from more drought-affected areas of origin.

title: When drought meets war trauma
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01909-5

The human consequences of armed conflict and climate change are often studied separately despite frequent co-occurrence of those events in fragile regions. A study now reveals a compounding effect of drought on post-traumatic stress from war, underlining the need for mental health services as a component of adaptation and humanitarian responses.

title: On the relevance of post-growth in China
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01889-6

Post-growth debates largely ignore China, despite its key position in the world economy, leaving a gap in sustainability discourse. This Perspective examines China’s role in a post-growth transition, comparing post-growth principles with China’s development model.

title: The politics of measuring sustainability progress and citizen science
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01899-4

Developing indicators, and the methodologies behind them, should make space for participatory approaches if we are to shape interventions equitably and effectively, argues Dilek Fraisl.

title: Navigating optimal solar-wind trade-offs under climate change
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75879-9

This study finds that climate change modestly alters optimal solar-wind ratios, whereas deployment pathways that diverge from climate-consistent optimal ratios can substantially increase electricity supply costs and capacity needs across regions.

title: Semiconductor room-temperature maser
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75446-2

The first semiconductor maser in silicon carbide is demonstrated, achieving continuous-wave operation above room temperature with high gain, microwave mode cooling, and ultrasensitive magnetometry, enabling compact, scalable maser technologies.

title: Highly scalable, dialysis-controlled synthesis of colloidal molecules via regulated self-assembly of polymer-grafted gold nanoparticles
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75712-3

Colloidal molecules mimic real molecules and can serve as nanoscale building blocks. Here, the authors use dialysis-guided aqueous self-assembly to produce them with high yield and concentration, highlighting their potential for hierarchical structure formation.

title: Scaling and Population Loss in Mexican Urban Centres
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75780-5

We analysed urban growth dynamics in 69 Mexican metropolitan areas from 1990 to 2020 using radial scaling analysis. In 30 years, the urban population shifted outwards, with all central zones losing 2.5 million people, absorbed by the peripheries.

title: Ecological novelty induced by climate change
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02697-8

The authors review ecological novelty—ecological situations with no precedent—arising from climate change. They discuss ecological novelty due to direct and indirect effects of climate change, and due to adaptation and mitigation measures, and explore management options that are against, for or tolerant of ecological novelty.

title: Global vessel carbon dioxide emission from navigable rivers
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02718-6

The magnitude and distribution of CO2 emissions from river transport are poorly constrained. This study finds that global CO2 emissions from inland vessels were about one-quarter of total vessel emissions, and that emissions were concentrated in the Northern Hemisphere, related to economic activity.

title: Multi-century cooling after net-zero greenhouse gas emissions
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02700-2

How global temperatures change after net-zero emissions are reached is highly uncertain. Here the authors constrain this response and find that net-zero GHG emissions lead to multi-century cooling of at least 0.6 °C.

title: Tracking the status of global evidence
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02720-y

Assessing the status of adaptation is important to target support and determine priority gaps. Here I look back on an influential 2021 study that reported a systematic review of evidence of implemented human adaptation and consider how this underscored the imperative for greater policy action and spawned methodological advancements in how to track adaptation progress.

title: Less than net zero needed to stabilize climate
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02708-8

Global temperature change over long times after cessation of greenhouse gas emissions is not well constrained. Now, research shows a consistent global cooling, especially if negative CO2 emissions compensate for continued CH4 and N2O emissions.

title: Geomagnetic storms caused by solar wind might be more extreme than previously thought
summary:
Nature, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02245-6

The severity of geomagnetic storms — magnetic disturbances in Earth’s outer atmosphere — is widely understood to reach an upper limit as the strength of the solar wind increases. But this upper limit is an illusion that results from uncertainty in the measurement of solar-wind strength as the true value regresses towards the mean.

title: Residents near small rivers in the USA could face disproportionately high future flood risk
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01905-9

Analysis combining high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations and demographic projections across the contiguous USA suggests that residents near small rivers face a disproportionately higher flood risk by 2050 than those near larger ones. This enhanced flood risk is mainly due to low defence levels and increases in projected flood magnitude under climate change.

title: Environmental impacts of Indigenous land restitution in Chile
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01876-x

Indigenous land restitution is often expected to deliver environmental co-benefits alongside redressing historical dispossession, but evidence of land-use change after restitution is limited. This study evaluates the land-use and environmental impacts of returning over 200,000 ha to Mapuche communities in Chile.

title: Evidence and limits of restitution
summary:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01850-7

Assessing whether returning land to Indigenous communities delivers on its environmental promise requires evidence that goes beyond titling of continuously occupied lands. A study now uses three decades of satellite data on Mapuche land restitution in Chile to show how restitution reshapes landscapes, but opens space to ask what such evidence can and cannot see.

title: AlphaGEM enables precise genome-scale metabolic modelling by integrating protein structure alignment with deep-learning-based dark metabolism mining
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75549-w

Building genome-scale metabolic models for less-characterized organisms remains challenging due to limited methods for reliable functional annotation. Here, the authors present AlphaGEM, a toolbox that integrates structural alignment and deep-learning approaches to improve protein relationship detection and expand metabolic networks, producing reconstructions that align with curated models across diverse species.

title: Pseudo point nodal superconducting gap in spin-triplet UTe<sub>2</sub>
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75566-9

The authors report thermal conductivity measurements on UTe2 down to 50 mK. From the data, they argue that UTe2 exhibits a fully-gapped state with a pseudo point-nodal structure, where gap minima along the b axis approach but never reach zero.

summary:

title: The Indian street dog crisis and multispecies coexistence in tropical urban futures
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00476-2

Cities in the Global South struggle with human–animal coexistence. This Perspective argues that, for free-ranging dogs in Indian cities, we are overlooking the ultimate issue, food subsidies that encourage and support dog packs and populations.

title: Urban climate vulnerability, housing and drug supply
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00490-4

Shifting illicit drug supplies and extreme weather patterns are heightening health risks for unhoused drug users in cities, but these dynamics are largely absent from climate planning. To address the compounded risks faced by this highly at-risk population, urban climate equity frameworks must integrate attention to the drug supply.

Control of the phase field is essential to enhance the efficiency of dielectric laser accelerator schemes. Here, the authors introduce a software-tunable approach to the optimization and control of the electron beams by combining spatial light modulators with pulsefront tilted beams.

title: Asymmetric temperature responses to soil moisture drought legacies under anthropogenic forcing
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75496-6

Annual soil water loss in the year after soil moisture droughts induces a larger annual warming effect than the annual cooling from an equivalent water gain.

title: Unravelling the key factors governing O<sub>2</sub> evolution upon charging a reversible LiOH-based nonaqueous Li | |O<sub>2</sub> battery
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75284-2

LiOH-based Li | |O2 batteries offer high energy density but suffer from poor reversibility. Here, authors study side-reaction origins and key reactive oxygen species during LiOH decomposition upon charge, and propose holistic strategies to effectively improve the Faradaic efficiency.

title: Unveiling surface and subsurface atomic vacancies in MoS<sub>2</sub> with lateral force microscopy
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 09 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75151-0

In this work, friction imaging is shown to detect atomic defects in MoS2, even when hidden below the surface, and to classify them through distinct friction fingerprints. This approach offers an accessible way to assess ultrathin material quality.

title: Co-benefit premiums can enhance nature-based climate solutions
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 08 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02690-1

Carbon markets reward the climate mitigation benefits of nature-based solutions but rarely value their broader societal impacts. Creating markets for verified co-benefits, such as coastal protection and biodiversity, could redirect investment towards projects that deliver larger gains for both people and climate.

title: Land-for-equity approach in Kigali’s informal transformation
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00473-5

The Mpazi rehousing project in Kigali shows how informal settlement upgrading can become feasible when informal land claims are formally valued and embedded within state- and donor-financed redevelopment, highlighting the institutional and financial conditions that make such models possible.

summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00470-8

Environmental DNA and associated techniques are transforming urban ecology and its conception of cities. Matthew Gandy argues for leveraging such ‘forensic ecologies’ for a post-positivist conceptual synthesis with the social and historical sciences.

summary:

A nuclear weapon orbiting Earth would emit neutrons through its interactions with the planet’s space radiation environment, and these could be detected by satellites.

summary:

Observations from satellites and climate-model simulations show that moderate volcanic eruptions and extreme wildfires have humidified the stratosphere since 2005. title: People systematically under- and overestimate public engagement in climate action
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02668-z

Unlike previous work showing that people underestimate others’ support for climate action, this study finds systematic pluralistic ignorance in both directions: frequent attitudes and actual behaviours are underestimated but rare ones are overestimated. This can be explained by general cognitive processes.

title: Future-proofing interpretations of the Paris Agreement’s limit of well below 2 °C
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02685-y

Here the authors show that a common interpretation of the Paris Agreement’s ‘well below 2° C’ target is changing with time, which could lead to higher overall warming. They propose that using median temperatures instead of probability ranges is more robust.

Nature Communications, Published online: 22 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74698-2

A study in mice and humans reveals that a placental enzyme AOC1 and the molecule spermidine help time labor through regulating autophagy. Boosting spermidine prevented preterm birth, suggesting a potential therapy for human premature labor.

title: Spatiotemporal modulation of surface texture for information encoding and object manipulation
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74794-3

Dynamic control of surface textures is limited by static or coarse-patterned approaches, restricting their application in programmable object manipulation and information encoding. This study achieved reversible, spatiotemporally programmable surface wrinkling on a photothermal liquid crystal elastomer bilayer, enabling precise, on-demand surface patterning, object propulsion, self-erasing information encoding, and reversible assembly processes through localized light stimuli.

title: Comprehensive national climate damage assessments framework applied to the UK
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02665-2

The economic impact of climate change has been widely acknowledged, yet current assessments remain fragmented and uncertain. Researchers develop a comprehensive channel-specific framework, apply it to the UK and show that the potential welfare loss could be much larger than previous estimates.

title: Climate change drives ecological novelty and new social challenges
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02672-3

Ecosystems are changing rapidly because of climate change, and this will have increasing social effects around the globe. We suggest that common social responses to rising novelty are often counterproductive, and we advocate for strategies that also allow for acceptance and adaptation to changes in nature.

title: Divergent surface urban heat island responses to background aerosol mitigation
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00463-7

Cities face co-occurring urban heat islands (UHIs) and air pollution, yet the impacts of aerosol cuts on urban–rural temperatures remain unclear. This study shows that cutting background aerosols strengthens summer UHIs in humid climates but weakens them in arid ones.

title: Advancing a biocultural vision for Nusantara
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00460-w

To achieve its ‘forest city’ ambitions, Nusantara needs to move beyond Indonesia’s exclusionary history of land governance and embrace a biocultural approach that centers its most affected human and nonhuman voices, recognizes customary rights, buttresses place-based livelihoods and advances environmental justice.

title: Wuliangye and Yibin
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00439-7

In Yibin, where two rivers merge into the Yangtze, the scent of grain from Wuliangye’s cellars has long been a kind of local weather. Now, as the city steps onto the national stage as a 2026 Spring Festival Gala sub-venue, I return to the confluence to ask what a hometown becomes when it is finally seen beyond the bottle.

title: Rethinking urban nature as technonature
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00471-7

Digitally mediated systems are transforming urban environments into continuously sensed and modulated ecologies, reshaping how nature is produced, governed and contested in cities.

summary:

summary:

Henipaviruses are a group of emerging human pathogens including the deadly Nipah virus. Here, the authors biochemically, biophysically, and structurally investigate the antigenicity and functionality of their surface glycoproteins.

summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74549-0

summary:

Nature Communications, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-71008-8

Authors reconstruct the molecular evolution of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) in East Asia. SFTSV splits into two lineages with diversity driven by segment-specific reassortment; transmission occurs via distinct networks.

title: Programmable multimodal actuation in cholesteric liquid crystal elastomer hollow fibers beyond mechanochromism
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-71050-6

Cholesteric liquid crystal elastomers are promising for color-changing soft robotics and photonic devices, though it is difficult to program their thermal or mechanical actuation. Here the authors design a hollow CLCE fiber system with tailored director alignments and preserving structural color.

title: Rapid subsurface warming in the subpolar North Atlantic from freshening
summary:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-70635-5

The North Atlantic subpolar gyre has freshened over recent decades, a trend projected to intensify under continued global warming. This study shows that the resulting increase in stratification drives ~ 1°C subsurface warming within a decade and a reorganisation of oceanic circulation that can enhance surface warming in the Nordic Seas.

title: Building façade photovoltaics enhance global climate resilience
summary:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02606-z

Façade-integrated photovoltaics (FIPV) present a promising yet early-stage solution for mitigating building emissions. Combining global building datasets, climate projections and façade-scale simulations, researchers estimate that FIPV could deliver substantial economic and climate benefits.

title: Datacenters as core infrastructure of urban AI
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00421-3

As datacenters enable urban AI, this Perspective argues that datacenters must be understood as core infrastructures, whose spatial distribution, governance arrangements, computational labor and economic logics reorganize urban space, redistribute power and externalize material costs, raising key challenges of energy justice, data sovereignty and civic accountability.

title: Understanding kampungs as critical urban infrastructures
summary:
Nature Cities, Published online: 27 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00428-w

Urban kampungs in Indonesia are more than ‘informal settlements’. They function as critical urban infrastructures that sustain climate resilience through distributed domesticity and enable inclusive governance through everyday social cooperation. This framing broadens the understanding of urban infrastructure beyond technical systems.

title: Urban nature equity must consider cultural nuances
summary:
npj Urban Sustainability, Published online: 12 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s42949-026-00352-x

Culture profoundly influences the way a person engages with nature. As cities rapidly increase in cultural diversity, achieving universal equity in access to nature and the benefits that flow from it will depend on meaningful consideration of this diversity in urban design. Current approaches to urban planning and design tend to be implicitly monocultural, which may diminish equity of access and reproduce entrenched epistemological and material conditions that contribute to power imbalances and dictate whose preferences are reflected in urban nature spaces. To move toward culturally inclusive urban nature design demands explicit efforts be made in policy and practice to embrace the contextual, dynamic and multifaceted nature of culture and resist the implicit adoption of monocultural urban nature designs. We discuss the consequences of superficial cultural inclusion attempts and propose three key recommendations for taking a culturally-conscious approach towards urban nature equity.

summary:

title: The Martian mid-latitude subsurface ice is the remnant of a past ice sheet
summary:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03418-x

Mars planetary climate model simulations show that mid-latitude ice accumulated around 630,000 years ago, at 35° obliquity, matching the depth and spatial variation of today’s buried ice and suggesting this ice layer contains a record of the retreating past surface ice sheet

title: A combination of social media and satellite data improves flood monitoring in China
summary:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 21 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03403-4

title: Land-atmosphere feedbacks and anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing intensify subseasonal drought-to-pluvial abrupt transitions
summary:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03371-9

title: Lake expansion underpinned the Silk Road prosperity during a drought period

Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 24 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03415-0

Enhanced meltwater in arid Central Asia during a warm and dry period in the Tang dynasty between CE 600 and 900 created well-watered corridors and supported Silk Road prosperity, according to a high-resolution lake-level record from Jili Lake, China
